issue_context.title: Node lifecycle controller does not `markPodsNotReady` when the node `Ready` state changes from `false` to `unknown`
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

When kubelet loses connect, the node goes into the unknown state. The node lifecycle controller marks the pod as not ready by the `markPodsNotReady` function because the health check status of the pod can not be obtained through kubelet. This feature is available only when node's `Ready` state transitions from `true` to `unknown`. 

However, if the node is already in the fail state (such as a containerd failure), `markPodsNotReady` will not take effect if the node loses its connection at this time.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cac53883f4714452f3084a22e4be20d042a9df33/pkg/controller/nodelifecycle/node_lifecycle_controller.go#L883-L888

In this case, the pod may accidentally remain ready, which may cause some network traffic to be accidentally forwarded to this node.

### What did you expect to happen?

As long as the node loses its connection beyond grace time, `MarkPodsNotReady` should always work

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Stop containerd and wait for the node `Ready` state to false
2. Stop kubelet or shutdown the node and wait the node `Ready` state to unknown
3. The pods which not be evicted on this node would be always ready

### Anything else we need to know?

In the node lifecycle controller logic,`MarkPodsNotReady` is just triggered when a node goes from `true` state to an `unknown` state. The correct way is to trigger when the node becomes `unknown` state regardless of whether the node state was previously true

review_comments: I was wondering why the addition of bool is needed here. Thanks in advance for the clarification!

In the original code, here were semantically misleading, giving the impression that markPodNotReady could be triggered if node switches status from True to non-True.  The lack of semantic clarity actually causes this bug.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0f8fb9f916d499137f16424c6891cf48547617b2/pkg/controller/nodelifecycle/node_lifecycle_controller.go#L878

In fact, We can trace the code. This conditional judgment is actually fully bound to tryUpdateNodeHealth, and only occurs if the Kubelet timeout to report a heartbeat and node was ready.  You might be surprised that markPodNotReady is not called when the node switches from Ready to False (But I have no intention of fixing this problem, see the comments above).

I hope the code here is more semantic and readable, so that the next time you modify it, you'll understand where markPodNotReady was decided. So I return this variable in the function and you can know I want to markPodsNotReady.

What if the condition changed from Ready -> NotReady. Shouldn't we also want to markPodsNotReady=true?

If I understand the change correctly, it seems this is only targeting the change if condition went to unknown state.

I would imagine the cases we want markPodsNotReady=true is if we from ready=true to ready=false or ready=Unknown, i.e:

Ready Condition (true) -> Ready Condition (false)
Ready Condition (true) -> Ready Condition (Unknown)

This is a good option to handle `false` state, and #112791 is modified in this way, but it can change existing behavior and cause a lot of UT failures. 

According to the unit test, false-> Unknow is undefined, so I just defined this behavior, which there's no impact on the original logic.

Marking pod NotReady makes sense when node `false`, because it cuts off network traffic faster. However, `false` is not as serious as `Unknown`, the container will probably survive and the network will still work. At `false` node , the HTTP readiness probe is usually still working and can report the `Ready` status of the pod (Exec Readiness probe may not work, but this can be a known limitation)

On the other hand, situations such as containerd upgrades can make kubelet to report node `false` in a short period of time (such as 10s) , which can cause the entire node's traffic to be cut off, which can be overly sensitive. 

So, I don't think it's necessary to handle `false` state in this bug fix at the moment, and we can require a new proposal to consider all scenarios.

IIRC, **only** Node in *Ready Condition (Unknown)* state, node-lifecycle-controller will mark Pods not-ready. And Node in *Ready Condition (False)* state, node-lifecycle-controller will **NOT** mark Pods not-ready.

Based on that, this PR codes could be more simpler and clearer?
